finding_reviews.rationale: Coverage holds: the nbhpc ledger has exactly one outstanding finding (this one, state remediation_pulled, no proposal). The FX01 condition now returns 0 of 110 non-USD private-credit rows at 2025-12-31 without principal_amount_usd. The three cited contexts c-936/c-937/c-938 publish GBP par 1,181/1,225/2,030 with cost 1,542/1,600/2,651 and fair value 1,592/1,652/2,737 thousand, matching the printed lines. Rejected on reasoning and next action. (1) The investigation says the whole-coupon reading for the SONIA rows needs 'the par-growth evidence the owner used' and routes the question to the owner as if that evidence were missing. It is in the cached filings and in the investigator's own sandbox. The same tranches print GBP 1,124 / 1,166 / 1,931 at 2025-06-30 and 2025-09-30, 1,181 / 1,225 / 2,030 at 2025-12-31 and 2026-03-31, and 1,238 / 1,284 / 2,127 at 2026-06-30. That is semi-annual capitalisation of 4.8 to 5.1 pct per half-year, about half of the printed 9.73 pct coupon, against about 3.0 pct for the 6.00 pct margin. This is the D-232 whole-coupon shape that earlier runs applied by row correction on par-growth evidence (D-246 'AX VI semi-annual'). It is not an open owner question. (2) The hypotheses miss a second published field on the cited rows that is not at a printed reading: coupon_type 'Fixed' on a loan printed 'SN + 6.00 %' with reference_rate_type SONIA. Next action should be: apply the D-232 whole-coupon reading to the SN rows on that par-growth evidence (row corrections, or the shared benchmark-list change with a cohort measurement), fix coupon_type, then re-run nbhp_retirements.py with the FX01 check restored.

observation_reviews.rationale: Verified in code: pipeline/whole_coupon_pik.py _BENCH has no 'SN', and 'S' followed by 'N' does not match, so HPS's 'SN + m % PIK c %' rows are not read, although the wrapper declares SN=SONIA in reference_rate_codes and pik_margin_reading whole_coupon (3b6c14ad). The proposed coverage report over declared reference codes is concrete. The statement that the SONIA rows' par growth 'has not been read' is a gap the investigator could have closed: see the FX01 review, where the same tranches compound about 4.8 to 5.1 pct per half-year. That does not change the detector decision.

Row corrections cannot set position_id, and reverting the names would re-publish wrong companies. Parking the two links for a shared matcher repair is the right route. The maturity-plus-par-ratio predicate is concrete and excludes ordinary amend-and-extend shapes.

The observation describes the carry-back as writing 'a company's later GICS industry heading' onto earlier rows. For structured credit that is false, and the carry-back spreads a wrong label backwards. From 2025-12-31 the filer prints the CLO notes under 'Structured Finance / Structured Finance Investments', directly after a 'Software' heading in the Unsecured Debt block. The printed-industry reader carries 'Software' into the CLO section, so all CLO rows from 2025-12-31 publish extracted_industry 'Software' and gics_sub_industry 'Application Software' (15/14/13 rows, 52.9/47.9/43.9M; already so in nvhpg). gics_industry_carry_back then copied 'Application Software' to 89 earlier rows of 14 CLO issuers (Voya CLO, Shackleton 2019-XV, Dryden 108, Monroe MML XVII, Bain 2024-3, 720 East V, ARES CLO, Columbia Cent 33, Rad CLO, Barings 2024-IV, BSP XXXVI, OCP 2024-33, Fort Washington 2019-1, ABPCI XVII). It replaced NULL, Diversified Financial Services or Multi-Sector Holdings. Every labelled structured-credit row 2023-03-31 to 2025-09-30 (22-63M a quarter) now carries Application Software; the rest stay NULL. The 'not_feasible' detection decision is wrong for this defect: a check that flags STRUCTURED_CREDIT rows with an operating-company sub-industry, or a printed-industry read that crosses a section heading, is cheap. The other 30 carried labels I sampled are plausible against the later printed GICS heading (QBS, Eisner, Solis, IP Operations, Sugar PPC, Zelis, Thrasio, Aurelia, Harp, Global Gruppe, Constellation, Bamboo, Meralm, Lackawanna, Dwyer, Madison Safety, Indigo, NDT, Summit, Wasserman, Artemis, NE SPV, Associations, Gusto, Vermont, Braya, Specialty Ingredients, More Cowbell, BLY, Alchemy). Separately, D-232 (b) was ruled 'opt-in for this fund only' for HPS Corporate Capital Solutions (D-232, D-236). Applying it to HPS Corporate Lending needs its own owner ruling, or at least a recorded D-207 orchestrator extension; the report records neither.
